subject: DPA clarifications - Aurora Tech
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications and next steps (Aurora Tech)

Hi Liam 

Thanks again for the discovery call today 

- great context on the fraud-detection pilot. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the DPA/privacy follow-ups you asked for and share next steps so we can keep your security team moving:

Summary of asks from Aurora:
- Clarify controller vs processor roles for model input/output and telemetry
- Subprocessors list and notification process for additions
- Breach/incident notification SLA (timing and scope)
- Data retention and log retention policies (PII, pseudonymization options)
- Data residency / EU hosting options
- SOC 2 report and any supporting evidence

Attachments: redwood-dpa.pdf (standard DPA), redwood-logging-matrix.xlsx (logging/retention mapping)

Quick answers and next steps (high level):
- Redwood acts as processor for customer-provided inputs and derived outputs; Aurora would be the controller for customer data and decisions. We can call out specifics in the DPA section 1.1 if you want explicit language.
- We maintain a published subprocessors page (link below) and provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; we can provide a current export as an appendix.
- Standard incident notification: initial acknowledgement within 24 hours; targeted notification with impact assessment within 72 hours for confirmed breaches affecting customer data. We can negotiate tighter timeline in enterprise agreements.
- Default log retention for hosted API telemetry is 90 days; high-sensitivity PII is not stored by default in text retention unless configured. We offer options for reduced retention, pseudonymization, and managed private deployments for full residency controls.
- EU-only residency is available via our Private deployment or via Dedicated EU region for enterprise customers.
- SOC 2 report and authorization evidence: happy to provide a current report under NDA / secure link.

Next step: Would it be OK to introduce Dev Patel (security engineer) for a 30-min technical call to walk through the logging matrix and any specific redlines Aurora's legal team has? Ben and I will also review your questionnaire and propose an appendix/redline to the DPA.

Thanks 

Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attached: redwood-dpa.pdf, redwood-logging-matrix.xlsx

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurora-tech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@aurora-tech.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps (Aurora Tech)

Thanks Marissa -

Appreciate the summary. A few follow-ups from our InfoSec and Legal teams (copied):

1) Controller/Processor: Can you confirm an explicit sentence we can include in the DPA that Redwood is a processor and Aurora is controller for all customer-supplied inputs and derived outputs? Our counsel prefers explicit callouts.

2) Subprocessors: Please send a current list (including cloud infra providers and any analytics vendors) and confirm the notification window for new subprocessors.

3) Breach notification: Our standard requirement is notification within 48 hours of discovery with ongoing updates. Can Redwood commit to 48h or is 72h the firm position? Also confirm scope - will you notify impacted customers directly or via a customer portal?

4) Retention and deletion: We need to understand how long raw inputs are retained, how long logs are kept, and whether you provide an API for deletion and verification. Specifically:
   - Raw inputs (user prompts and files)
   - Model outputs (generated text)
   - Telemetry/logs (request metadata, latency, error traces)

5) Data residency: For EU customers we require that data never leaves the EU for processing/storage. Is there an EU-hosted option that guarantees this for both live inference and backups?

6) SOC 2: Please share the latest report or a link so our team can validate.

Attached our internal security questionnaire (aurora-security-questionnaire.xlsx) - some items are duplicates of the above but the auditor likes the form.

Also - will Redwood accept a few DPA redlines from our counsel or do you require that we use your standard DPA?

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Product Security, Aurora Tech
liam.oconnor@aurora-tech.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps (Aurora Tech)

Hi Liam -

Thanks for the concrete list - diving in inline below. Happy to jump on a call with your security team.

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed - Redwood acts as the processor. We are happy to add explicit language to section 1.1 of the DPA that states: "Redwood Inference shall process Customer Data only on behalf of and in accordance with Customer's documented instructions. Customer is the Controller for Customer Data." If you want a slightly different phrasing, send counsel's suggested sentence and we will review.

2) Subprocessors: Our current subprocessors include (summary): AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1 where applicable), GCP (for Dedicated partners), Datadog (ops telemetry), S3-compatible storage providers. Full list and contractual scopes are on our subprocessors page: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors. We provide a 30-day notice for material additions and an exportable list on request. We can include the current export as an appendix to the DPA.

3) Breach notification: Our standard commitment is initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of detection and targeted notification including impact assessment within 72 hours for confirmed incidents. We understand Aurora's 48-hour ask; we will escalate internally to see if we can commit to a 48-hour initial notification for this engagement. For clarity: notifications are sent directly to the customer security contacts (and to any designated legal contact). We also publish incident advisories to our secure customer portal for post-incident details.

4) Retention and deletion: Default behaviors (hosted API):
   - Raw inputs: not retained beyond request processing unless customer enables retention for fine-tuning or evaluation. When retention is enabled, retention period defaults to 30 days unless otherwise negotiated.
   - Model outputs: retained only if retention is enabled; otherwise not persisted beyond response streaming.
   - Telemetry/logs: request metadata and traces retained 90 days by default; we can reduce this to 30 or 7 days for high-sensitivity customers or move logs to a private deployment.
We expose admin APIs for data deletion requests and provide verification artifacts on request (audit logs showing deletion). We can scope retention and deletion requirements in an appendix to the DPA. See attached logging matrix for column-level mapping.

5) Data residency: We offer EU-only residency for both processing and storage via our Private deployment or Dedicated EU region. For hosted customers in the US region, data is processed and stored in us-east by default and may be replicated for backups; EU residency guarantees are only available under a dedicated/private deployment with contractual controls.

6) SOC 2: We can provide the current SOC 2 Type II report via secure link or NDA. See link below; we will also put a copy on the secure drive for your team.

Next steps:
- Dev Patel (cc) can run a 30-minute technical review with your security engineer next week to walk the logging matrix and discuss deletion APIs.
- Marissa and I will draft an appendix to the DPA with the retention and subprocessors export and share a proposed small set of redlines for legal to review. If Aurora has firm DPA redlines, please send them and we will review; we typically negotiate a few clause-level items on enterprise deals.

Links/attachments included: redwood-dpa-appendix.pdf; redwood-logging-matrix.xlsx; https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors; https://redwood.example.com/soc2-report

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
